arguments.prompt:
Create ORIGINAL purpose-drawn high-detail PIXEL ART game sprite animation on a truly TRANSPARENT RGBA background. No floor, no shadow disc, no checkerboard, no lettering, no labels, no panels or cell lines. Exactly FOUR COLUMNS. Every cell contains exactly ONE complete full-body figure (with complete held equipment). Side/three-quarter view facing RIGHT consistently. Natural anatomy, readable hands, constant costume and body proportions. Each pose genuinely different, not repeated or mirrored copies. Every cell independently has at least12% clear transparent padding above head, below SHOE SOLES and around hands/weapon/effects. Keep last-row feet well ABOVE the canvas edge: all toes, soles, robe and coat tails entirely visible. Nothing crosses cell or row seams. Never zoom a crouching pose up to standing height; keep the same anatomical size across the source. Small spell flashes remain local; large runtime projectiles must not be drawn as separate distant objects in these actor cells. Reference is an older approximate sprite identity; follow explicit version/costume/weapon corrections over its erroneous props or poses.
PORTRAIT ATLAS EXACTLY4 columns by8 rows,32 complete poses, aspect ratio1:2. Every row is a different specified phase in this exact order.
IDENTITY/VERSION: Rupert Giles, middle-aged human Watcher in Buffy season7. Short receding brown/grey hair, rectangular wire glasses, brown tweed jacket over grey waistcoat and pale shirt, dark red tie, brown trousers and sensible brown shoes. Physical wooden-and-dark-metal CROSSBOW with horizontal bow limbs and visible bolt rail; held in TWO hands. No gun, magical book laser or huge fantasy bow.
SOURCE SUPER: Couverture à l’arbalète de Giles; effect damage, delivery projectile. It is an adaptation of the source action, not an official animation reproduction.
ROW1 intro: INTRO: enter right-facing with weapon/hand lowered, adjust clothing or grip, look ahead, set composed ready stance. Four distinct full-body poses.
ROW2 outro: OUTRO: release ready stance, lower hands/weapon safely, turn shoulder slightly away while still oriented right, step to leave. Four different poses, no copied intro frames.
ROW3 roundVictory: ROUND VICTORY: straighten from a low ready position, small confident nod, restrained raised free hand, return to guarded stance. Distinct from final victory.
ROW4 roundDefeat: ROUND DEFEAT: surprised but uninjured pause, bend knees and catch breath, one hand briefly supports a knee, rise toward ready stance. No wounds or unconscious body.
ROW5 fatality: FINALE (adapted non-execution): Crossbow cover: bring the held crossbow up, shoulder and aim along its bolt rail to the RIGHT, release a physical bolt with a tiny local string snap, lower the crossbow. Do not draw a distant flying bolt or long energy trail. Muzzle/bolt-rail tip remains clear and separate from hands. Finale variant braces a half-step lower and sights carefully before release, then lowers.
ROW6 victory: VICTORY: relax shoulders, warm or reserved source-appropriate acknowledgment, lower hands while shifting rear foot, composed final gesture. No personality-breaking celebration or copied roundVictory.
ROW7 defeat: DEFEAT: tired protective posture, lower to one knee while keeping equipment safe, look down and breathe, begin to rise. Non-graphic, all feet and clothing intact.
ROW8 super: SUPER: Crossbow cover: bring the held crossbow up, shoulder and aim along its bolt rail to the RIGHT, release a physical bolt with a tiny local string snap, lower the crossbow. Do not draw a distant flying bolt or long energy trail. Muzzle/bolt-rail tip remains clear and separate from hands. Use the principal sequence; the alternative braces a half-step lower and sights carefully before release, then lowers.
Again EXACTLY8 rows with4 distinct poses each. Do not crop the bottom row. Keep whole weapon, shoes and any local spell inside each cell. No additional characters or objects.
